scope: Corollary D.7 (Characters for a tilted height) of the manuscript “Uniform Cartier sections for Fano type contractions” (preprints/Uniform-Cartier-sections-for-Fano-type-contractions-September-25-2026/Uniform-Cartier-sections-for-Fano-type-contractions-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 066 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8d97ba60373419ba), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 61. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose there are boundedly many invariant rational eigenfunctions Y ± j of weights ±kj, with hmj Y ± j ∈ R̆, 0 < mj ≤ ALj, 1 ≤ Lj ≤ L, where A is fixed. Fix bounded real numbers uj and δ > 0. Assume that, at every nonzero pure weight and at all Gauss extensions over primitive P with a(P) = 0, LD(P) → 0, the evaluations satisfy yj = v(Y + j ) = −v(Y − j ), ∑︂ j ujyj Lj ≤ δv(h). (D.20) It suffices to check these inequalities on rational vectors. For fixed M0 sufficiently large compared with 1/δ, choose integers rj = M0ujL/Lj + O(1), with uniformly bounded rounding errors. Then there is a regular nonzero symbol of finite-group character χqm and torus weight q ⎛ ⎝mu − ∑︂ j rjkj ⎞ ⎠ , 0 < m ≤ C6M0δL, (D.21) for a bounded positive integer q. The constant C6 depends only on the fixed bounds for the number of functions, their costs, the uj, and rounding errors; it is independent of δ and M0. The bound for q may depend on the fixed choices δ, M0. No order condition (C.5) is assumed here.
